{{Short description|Computationally feasible measure in real-valued number of dimensions}}
The '''Minkowski [[content (measure theory)|content]]''' (named after [[Hermann Minkowski]]), or the '''boundary measure''', of a set is a basic concept that uses concepts from [[geometry]] and [[measure theory]] to generalize the notions of [[arc length|length]] of a [[smooth curve]] in the plane, and [[surface area|area]] of a smooth surface in [[euclidean space|space]], to arbitrary [[measurable set]]s. 

It is typically applied to [[fractal]] boundaries of domains in the [[Euclidean space]], but it can also be used in the context of general metric [[Measure space|measure spaces.]]

It is related to, although different from, the [[Hausdorff measure]].
<!--== Definition ==
Let <math>\scriptstyle(X,\, \mu,\, d)</math> be a metric measure space, where ''d'' is a [[metric (mathematics)|metric]] on ''X'' and &mu; is a [[Borel measure]]. For a subset ''A'' of ''X'' and real &epsilon; > 0, let

<math display="block">A_\varepsilon = \{ x \in X \, | \, d(x, A) \leq \varepsilon \}</math>

be the &epsilon;-''extension'' of ''A''. The '''lower Minkowski content''' of ''A'' is given by

<math display="block">M_*(A) = \liminf_{\varepsilon \to 0} \frac{\mu(A_\varepsilon) - \mu(A)}{\varepsilon},</math>

and the '''upper Minkowski content''' of ''A'' is

<math display="block">M^*(A) = \limsup_{\varepsilon \to 0} \frac{\mu(A_\varepsilon) - \mu(A)}{\varepsilon}.</math>

If ''M''<sub>*</sub>(''A'')&nbsp;=&nbsp;''M''<sup>*</sup>(''A''), then the common value is called the '''Minkowski content''' of ''A'' associated with the measure &mu;, and is denoted by ''M''(''A'').-->
<!-- old section header being replaced with Definition, as original section commented above is not in either source.... == Minkowski content in '''R'''<sup>''n''</sup> ==-->

==Definition==
For <math> A \subset \mathbb{R}^{n}</math>, and each integer ''m'' with <math> 0 \leq m \leq n</math>, the '''''m''-dimensional upper Minkowski content''' is

<math display="block">M^{*m}(A) = \limsup_{r \to 0^+} \frac{\mu(\{x: d(x,A) < r\})}{\alpha (n-m)r^{n-m}}</math>

and the '''''m''-dimensional lower Minkowski content''' is defined as

<math display="block">M_*^m(A) = \liminf_{r \to 0^+} \frac{\mu(\{x: d(x,A) < r\})}{\alpha (n-m)r^{n-m}}</math>

where <math>\alpha(n-m)r^{n-m}</math> is the volume of the [[N-sphere|(''n''&minus;''m'')-ball]] of radius r and <math>\mu</math> is an <math>n</math>-dimensional [[Lebesgue measure]]. 

If the upper and lower ''m''-dimensional Minkowski content of ''A'' are equal, then their common value is called the Minkowski content ''M''<sup>''m''</sup>(''A'').<ref>{{harvnb|Federer|1969|p=[https://books.google.com/books?id=jld-BgAAQBAJ&pg=PA273 273]}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Krantz|Parks|1999|loc=[https://books.google.com/books?id=sADLB3ybGS0C&pg=PA74 p. 74]}}</ref>

== Properties ==
* The Minkowski content is (generally) not a measure.  In particular, the ''m''-dimensional Minkowski content in '''R'''<sup>n</sup> is not a measure unless ''m''&nbsp;=&nbsp;0, in which case it is the [[counting measure]].  Indeed, clearly the Minkowski content assigns the same value to the set ''A'' as well as its [[closure (topology)|closure]].
* If ''A'' is a closed ''m''-[[rectifiable set]] in '''R'''<sup>''n''</sup>, given as the image of a bounded set from '''R'''<sup>''m''</sup> under a [[Lipschitz function]], then the ''m''-dimensional Minkowski content of ''A'' exists, and is equal to the ''m''-dimensional [[Hausdorff measure]] of ''A''.<ref>{{harvnb|Federer|1969|p=275, Theorem 3.2.39}}</ref>
